Definition: the liver (as the heaviest of the viscera)
BiblicalUsage: Kabed is the liver — the heaviest of the inner organs, and the one the law names again and again in the sacrifices. The fat upon the liver was burned on the altar with the peace offering and the sin offering, and the proverb pictures a young man following temptation like an arrow striking the liver.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the liver matters because God claimed the inward parts for Himself. The sacrifices were not only outward show; the fat and the inward parts went up to Him, and that is how I understand worship — God wants the inside, not only the outside.
